q: A function f: ℝ → ℝ has the Luzin N-property if:
opts: f maps null sets to null sets
f maps null sets to sets of positive measure
exp: Luzin N: f maps every Lebesgue-null set to a null set. Absolutely continuous functions satisfy Luzin N (this is key to the fundamental theorem of calculus for Lebesgue integrals), but the converse fails.
